reviews.text: Played the demo and was extremely fun and addictive. Cannot wait to continue playing it.

Played about 30 min and im already hooked. You hover over the monsters to fire and the weapons bounce around doing the damage, really satisfying to watch. Not fully afk early on, you still gotta aim a bit before automating is unlocked, but its super low stress. Good fun so far, gonna keep playing.

说一下不推荐的理由： 1.游戏从头到尾没有爽感，所有升级都被设计师固定了，你玩这个游戏没有任何意外，到了哪一步该干什么都是固定死了，所以非常非常枯燥，重复感太高了； 2.中文翻译简直一坨，全是乱码； 3.看着有5中武器，实际上效果都差不多，也没有什么联动机制，包括每种武器的天赋树都差不多一样； 4.提升最大实际上只有铁匠铺，也就是花钱提升攻击力，但是，这个设定非常迷，每升级5次还是6次来着会有一个1.3倍的乘数提升，实际上你的提升全靠这个1.3倍提升。前面5次升级我没记错的话每次只加2点攻击！打一个怪100多块钱，你需要花费几万块钱提升2点攻击，还不如直接花5倍价钱直接1.3倍攻击算了，完全没有意义； 5.遗物系统也很迷，遗物系统是靠武器弹射次数来触发，其中有一个遗物本身没有特殊效果，他的作用就是使另外两个遗物效果再次触发，但是问题就在这，这个遗物触发效果的同时，另外两个遗物的进度条也会清零，就很迷。 总之，是一款一直坐牢的游戏，怪物的数量和生成速度很慢，但是怪物血量提升远远大于你伤害提升，就导致你虽然一直再爬层数，但是，实际上区别不大。目前不建议入手。

It too me just under 3 hours to complete the game, for what ever reason non of the achievements unlocked but there is no chance I will play through the game again to get them. You start out with a single weapon that tracks your mouse location to target the mobs, later you unlock the ability to "wake" areas that will also target enemies for your weapon to target. This is as far as it gets when it comes to Idle gameplay. Later you unlock more weapon types, at some point the weapons projectiles fill the screen so much that you cant see the nice pixel art this game has, it becomes just a mess. The tech tree does not feel satisfying to use, the later unlocks towards game progression feel useless & unsatisfying. Their is no prestige mechanic, instead it has a straight forward endgame mechanic that also feels like a short time sync and a meaningless step forward to the end goal of clearing floor 30. If the game is on sale and you see 3 hours of active gameplay with unsatisfying gameplay worth the price, than buy it. Otherwise save your money.

I was looking forward to play this game after playing the Demo a while ago, but I have to put some thoughts about the release here for people to see what they will get: The game is easily finished in 3h and there is not an endless scaling, so after 3h you are done. I really liked the game mechanics in the demo, and they stayed the same for the release, BUT there were little to no new mechanics and not much new content in general (Demo was about 50% of the game). So if you played the Demo and are looking to grind the full release for hours, you can't. The game has good potential and if the dev(s) keep working on it with new content updates, I would love to grind it. But as of now, everybody has to know if they want to spend 5 bucks for 3h content.

This is one of the worst games in this genre. There are enemies in a box, something you can upgrade kills them and you get gold, then you move on to a stage with harder enemies that drop more gold. The "twist" with this game to make it stand out is the thing you use to kill enemies is a weapon that bounces around the screen and shoots an arrow at your cursor. After about 15 minutes this is no longer relevant as you have unlocked methods to kill enemies without needing to mouse over them. The main reason this is so bad compared to the many other copies of the exact same format is the terrible balancing and lack of care. In earlier stages, the enemies increase in health so much that you are actually making less gold by advancing than you would be staying at that previous stage. Its something like a 3-4x hp increase with a 25% gold increase, obviously not worth it. The damage upgrade is a flat +2 dmg 6 times, then a 1.2x multiplier. This exact same cycle repeats. The flat damage never changes, so at later stages it doesnt affect your damage at all until you get to the multiplier. There are so many examples of poor balance that I cant possibly fit them all here. Other issues include the game not being resizable, the game pausing when you are tabbed out, upgrade names being wrong, higher tiers of upgrades being worse than the previous tiers, the game introducing a system with a tutorial box about 20 minutes before you unlock that system, 2 of the final 3 systems having almost no effect on gameplay at all, etc. It feels like a cheap cash grab. The dev clearly didnt even bother to do a full playthrough before releasing it (even though its only 2 or 3 hours long).

I'm recommending it to those who like incremental games. I personally was rather frustrated that there weren't more options for automation, but the game doesn't bill itself that way, so that's just a selfish frustration. If you're looking to while away a few hours to 100% a game, this isn't a bad choice.

After completing all achievements, I can say this isn't worth your time or money. The gameplay loop quickly became monotonous. There's no real strategic choices to make past the first hour. I ran into multiple graphical glitches. Some buttons wouldn't click for me until I tried another button first. One of the weapons had a sound effect that bothered me, but there's no way to turn down just the sound effects, unless you disable the graphical part of the effects too. I got this during the introductory sale for $4.49 and played for about three hours. The second half was monotonous to the point that the first half was no longer enjoyable. I'd be hesitant to suggest it if it were free. It's not bad per say, again just not worth your time.

The game feels extremely unpolished, upgrade names don't match effect, tutorial lies to you, UI has overlaps, buttons not always work, not all sound effects are bound to the options sliders, I had to mute the game on system level to get rid of annoying sound effect for the last weapon. Gameplay wise, it's kind of ok. Bouncy weapons are fun to watch for a bit and then the game ends. There is not much choice in the gameplay, mechanics are simple and don't offer more than you immediatelly see. They are scattered through progression so at least there is some sense of progression offered. There are tons of better games with similar pricetag in the genre, this is passable if you already played the better ones.

Poor progression, broken RNG, not worth your time. A 25% success rate sounds manageable until you've failed it fifteen times in a row, each failure adding 5 more tokens to an already punishing cost. I'm currently sitting at 80 tokens required just to attempt a repair, with no guarantee of anything but more grinding. What makes it worse is the obvious imbalance: crafting upgrade success rates decrease with each tier, yet the repair chance stays at a flat 25%. That's not a difficulty curve, that's just tedium dressed up as a mechanic.

The good: Very cool and intense incremental game. You will spend hours with this one! Upgrading all the skills and damage, is consistent and done regularly. You always have something to do. You also have agency over whats happening in the arena, your mouse is used to debuff the targets heavily, that step inside a rings system, that keeps you focused into damaging the biggest groups you can. This is NOT an idle game like some potatoes are crying about, this is an INCREMENTAL game, with actually stuff to do while the game runs. The smart: You can visually disable weapon graphics and/or their visual effects! This is a great option, screen more clear, better fps, less heat build up on console. I wish all Devs had this at least in their TODO code comments. The meh: It's incomplete in terms of UI, but worse, on UX (user experience). One single example: there is no welcome screen, well, nothing more than the game starting immediately, and off you go. Users may feel that this is an incomplete game, probably the reason why so many salty rants around here, but, this is a game done and ready to play until the end.

Oh my god, no. This is a buggy mess. I'll list the bugs I've found in my play and from checking the community forums: There's a plinko machine (The thing where you drop the balls down the top, they bounce off the pegs and hit the scores at the bottom) the bar for that gets bigger as you pick up little purple orbs. It eventually stretches across your screen. It's not supposed to. The values at the bottom. 3X 4X 5X 4X 3X are supposed to increase with various talents. They only increase a couple times, then just stop bothering. The game does not save for everyone... this is a major one, you have to get all the achievements in one go if that's what you're doing. Every time you close and open the game, you will have to start over. The game did save for me. But for a lot of people on the forums, it doesn't save. Sometimes common enemies join the bosses. They're not supposed to. They also join the vault enemies. Again, not supposed to. The notification to upgrade your weapons doesn't go away once they're all fully upgraded. You can still buy skill points even when you have all the skills. For some people on the forums, achievements don't work, I didn't have this issue myself, but be warned, that's also a possible thing. The usual fix for broken achievements on a steam game is to close and re-open the game, but as mentioned before... that's a really bad idea. These are all bugs... This is before I get into just how boring the game itself is. The game involves a weapon bouncing off the sides of the screen, something you'll want to turn off the effects for in the options fairly quickly, because as you get more of these, it's visually vexing. You move your cursor over the various enemies and they get hit by the weapons. You do get blue circles that automate this for you... but don't go thinking this game then becomes an idle game, no, you're not so lucky. You have to wake up the blue circles by mousing over them and they only last a short time. There are skill trees and weapon upgrades and upgrades for your circles. The game does have plenty of upgrades. The main issue is that a lot of upgrades are useless. For instance, you can increase how many iron bars drop.... but iron bars are only useful for the first two weapons, and once they're maxed they're never useful ever again. This is the same for every other bar. Once you finally get to the end of the game and beat the last boss, the game shows you some basic statistics. Some of which are irrelevant because of course you have 4 relics, that's the maximum you can equip... And only offers you one choice.... Quit. No keep playing (Why would you want to I guess? Even the developer knows you want to stop playing.) No endless mode, nope... Just quit. Quit and uninstall I suppose. I did manage to get all the achievements... Which is a good thing, but unfortunately for some people, some achievements don't work. So this game is not worth your time if you want it for the game, or for the achievements. This game is never worth anyones time or money. Also... seriously? £5?! That's a lot of money for this utter wank. But even if it were on a 99% off sale, it still wouldn't be worth it. It's broken, it's terrible, it's a waste of time. And not in a good way. It's a shame, it's a fun idea and if done well it could've been a good game.... it just isn't. Thanks for reading, or skipping to the end. Have a lovely day. <3

This is a game that I would like quite a bit if they made a couple simple changes, doesn't look like they will because no patches since release. The biggest one is that you can't actually mute the game. There is a music volume slider, but the in game sound effects can't be completely muted (you can remove some by changing the display but not everything is affected). Several of the upgrades don't actually do anything or don't do what they say, the game is incredibly manual and just a bit of a slog to get all the way through. Luckily it is a short game, if it was much longer I wouldn't have bothered to finish it. Also it is worth mentioning that the actual game is a bit different from the video. You can never have more than one of each weapon and the max level is 30.
